comment: What a scene leaves behind, and for how long.
AAF tells us what an animation WAS through its tags -- the same vocabulary the
animation packs are written in. The tags below are matched without regard to
case against every animation of a scene, and the sets they name are applied to
both actors when the scene ends. A scene whose tags match nothing here leaves
nothing behind, which is what makes kissing and foreplay free: they simply have
The sets themselves are defined in Data/AAF/Rapport_overlayData.xml and carry no
AAF duration, so AAF never removes them. Rapport removes them, in game hours,
from the save -- which is the whole reason this is a framework feature and not
Who receives what is decided by the set, not by this file: each set has a female
and a male condition and AAF picks the one that fits the actor.
comment_backend: Which mod's art Rapport drives. Two do this job and they share nothing:
CumOverlays paints a flat LooksMenu texture on the body, Commonwealth
Moisturizer equips a BodySlide-conformed mesh and swaps morphing headparts
for the face. The mesh has actual volume and is the only one of the two that
does faces at all, so "auto" prefers it when both are installed.
Rapport drives ONE of them and silences BOTH. The backend chooses which mod's
art gets applied, not which one is allowed to keep applying its own: a mod
left listening to AAF goes on painting the same bodies on its own schedule,
which is exactly the collision this setting exists to avoid. Both are started
again when aftermath is switched off.
comment_layers: How much, in the one place it landed. Moisturizer puts ONE decal per region
per call, and its own picker skips slots that are already used rather than
re-rolling them -- so three calls means three distinct decals, not the same
one three times. It only wipes and starts over once a region is full.
This is the 'a lot of cum' knob. It stacks in ONE place because the place is
the last hole the scene touched; spreading it over every hole a long scene
passed through was the wrong reading of 'a lot'.
Overlay backend ignores this: quantity is set per set in
comment_regions: Moisturizer's API takes three places rather than named sets: front, oral,
rear. This says which of them each set corresponds to, so the tag mapping
below drives both backends instead of being written out twice.
comment_hours: How long it stays visible, in GAME hours. 12 is most of a day: long enough to
still be there after the walk home, short enough not to be permanent. Real
time is the wrong unit -- a player who sleeps eight hours should not find it
unchanged, and one who stands still for ten minutes should.
comment_climax: With requireClimax on, a scene leaves nothing behind unless an animation
tagged Climax actually played. That is more faithful and much rarer: many
packs never tag a climax at all, so the honest default is off.
